result:
I found one real bug: `AdlLexer` slows down quadratically on long lines (a ReDoS-style denial-of-service issue). The report is in `bug_report_pygments_lexers_archetype_2026-10-06_01-13_ihdf.md`.

**The bug (Medium):** the ADL lexer has no rule for ordinary words, or for spaces and tabs not followed by a newline. Each such character becomes its own `Error` token. Before each one, several regexes rescan the rest of the run, so doubling the input roughly quadruples the time:

| Input | 5,000 chars | 10,000 chars | 20,000 chars |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"a" * n` | 0.70 s | 2.71 s | 11.3 s |
| `" " * n + "x"` | 0.59 s | 2.36 s | 9.58 s |

So about 20 KB of untrusted text takes roughly 10 seconds of CPU. That matters for any service that highlights `.adl` files or calls `guess_lexer` on user input. `OdinLexer` and `CadlLexer` handle the same inputs in about 1 ms.

**Test results:**
- **Round-trip** (joining the tokens gives back the input) passed 2,000 examples across all three lexers.
- **A general timing test** on repeated short patterns, run on all three lexers, passed. It didn't catch the bug because its inputs were too short to cross the 2-second threshold.
- **A focused scaling test** failed on `ch='a'`: 4× the input (2,000 → 8,000 characters) took about 13× as long.

**Fix:** add two rules to the end of the `AdlLexer` `root` state: `(r'[ \t]+', Whitespace)` and `(r'\w+', Text)`. I tested this as a subclass rather than editing the source, and the 20,000-character cases dropped from about 10 s to about 2 ms. The report also suggests changing `\.\w+[\w-]*\.v` in the archetype-ID regex to `\.\w[\w-]*\.v`, because the two overlapping quantifiers cause extra backtracking.

The tests are in `test_archetype.py`.

Separately, several claude.ai connectors (Asana, Atlassian, Box, Canva, Figma, HubSpot, Intercom, Linear, Notion, monday.com) need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This run didn't need them.
